# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

# gba-emu build plan

Goal: an original Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust, built as `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, exporting the 10
functions in `gba-eval/spec/ABI.md`, that scores above the 0.534 baseline on the gba-eval grader. The
grader's highest reachable score is 0.96, because the `comprehensive` subsystem carries weight but has no tests.

Paths in this document are relative to this repo (`gba-trial/gba-emu`). The benchmark repo is
`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.

## Scope: must-have vs stretch

| Phases | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | **Must-have** | Skeleton, CPU, interrupts/timers/DMA, full graphics. Each one finished, gated and verified with a milestone grade before the next starts. |
| 4-6 | **Stretch** | Sound, game compatibility/timing, performance. Started only once Phase 3 is verified, and dropped if time runs out. |

A solid, verified 0-3 is worth more than a broken 0-6. Never start a stretch phase while a
must-have gate is failing, and never leave `main` in a state that does not build or that scores lower
than the last milestone.

---

## 1. How the score is made (what to optimise)

| Section | Weight | Tests | Scoring |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replay | 60% | 11 homebrew games with recorded input | Mean per-frame SSIM vs Mesen2 over thousands of frames. Drifting out of sync ruins every later frame. |
| Procedural | 20% | 16 test ROMs | Only the final frame counts, and it must be almost pixel-exact (pass/fail). |
| Audio | 20% | 9 of the replays | Per-frame log-mel spectrum vs Mesen2. Silence scores 0. |

Procedural subsystem weights: cpu 0.35, comprehensive 0.20 (no tests, always 0), memory 0.15,
timer 0.12, halt_irq 0.10, dma 0.08. Audio: psg 0.5, game_audio 0.5.

Consequences:
- **CPU correctness comes first.** Every other test depends on it.
- **The PPU (graphics) carries the most weight**, because all 11 replays are graphics comparisons.
- **Timing accuracy matters a lot**, because replay inputs land on fixed frame numbers. If the game boots
  a few frames later than in Mesen2, every button press lands at the wrong moment.
- **Colour precision is forgiving.** The grader quantises to 5 bits per channel, so any sensible
  5-to-8-bit colour expansion is fine.

---

## 2. Architecture and shared contracts (Phase 0, one agent, before any parallel work)

Everything that more than one agent touches is defined here first. Parallel agents then work only inside
their own files, which is what keeps merges conflict-free.

One crate, `gba_emu`, with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`. The `rlib` lets `cargo test` and a native
debug binary run on the host without wasm.

```
src/
  lib.rs          ABI exports only (the 10 functions), thin wrappers over a single global Gba
  gba.rs          Gba struct: owns every component, run_frame() main loop
  bus.rs          memory map: read8/16/32, write8/16/32, region dispatch, returns access cycles
  io.rs           IO register dispatch table: address range -> owning component
  irq.rs          IE / IF / IME, request(IrqSource), pending() -> bool
  scheduler.rs    cycle counter; components are stepped by "cycles elapsed"
  cpu/mod.rs      Cpu struct, register file, modes, banking, CPSR/SPSR, exceptions, step()
  cpu/alu.rs      barrel shifter, add/sub with flags, condition evaluation
  cpu/arm.rs      ARM (32-bit) decode + execute
  cpu/thumb.rs    THUMB (16-bit) decode + execute
  ppu/mod.rs      line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT/VCOUNT, line compositor, framebuffer
  ppu/bg_text.rs  tiled backgrounds (modes 0-2)
  ppu/bg_affine.rs rotation/scaling backgrounds
  ppu/bitmap.rs   modes 3/4/5
  ppu/obj.rs      sprites (normal + affine)
  ppu/effects.rs  windows, blending, mosaic
  timer.rs        4 timers, prescaler, cascade, overflow IRQ, FIFO tick
  dma.rs          4 DMA channels, triggers, priority
  apu/mod.rs      mixer, SOUNDCNT/SOUNDBIAS, output buffer, sample rate
  apu/psg.rs      channels 1-4
  apu/fifo.rs     direct sound channels A/B
  keypad.rs       KEYINPUT / KEYCNT
  cart.rs         ROM, save memory (SRAM / Flash / EEPROM), GPIO
src/bin/run_rom.rs  native debug tool: run a ROM for N frames, write the frame as .ppm and audio as .wav
```

Contracts fixed in Phase 0:

Special features of the separate DMA channels
DMA0 - highest priority, best for timing critical transfers (eg. HBlank DMA).
DMA1 and DMA2 - can be used to feed digital sample data to the Sound FIFOs.
DMA3 - can be used to write to Game Pak ROM/FlashROM (but not GamePak SRAM).
Aside from that, each DMA 0-3 may be used for whatever general purposes.

40000BCh,0BEh - DMA1SAD - DMA 1 Source Address (W) (any memory)
40000C8h,0CAh - DMA2SAD - DMA 2 Source Address (W) (any memory)
40000D4h,0D6h - DMA3SAD - DMA 3 Source Address (W) (any memory)
The most significant address bits are ignored, only the least significant 27 or
28 bits are used (max 07FFFFFFh internal memory, or max 0FFFFFFFh any memory -
except SRAM ?!).

40000B4h,0B6h - DMA0DAD - DMA 0 Destination Address (W) (internal memory)
40000C0h,0C2h - DMA1DAD - DMA 1 Destination Address (W) (internal memory)
40000CCh,0CEh - DMA2DAD - DMA 2 Destination Address (W) (internal memory)
40000D8h,0DAh - DMA3DAD - DMA 3 Destination Address (W) (any memory)
The most significant address bits are ignored, only the least significant 27 or
28 bits are used (max. 07FFFFFFh internal memory or 0FFFFFFFh any memory -
except SRAM ?!).

40000B8h - DMA0CNT_L - DMA 0 Word Count (W) (14 bit, 1..4000h)
40000C4h - DMA1CNT_L - DMA 1 Word Count (W) (14 bit, 1..4000h)
40000D0h - DMA2CNT_L - DMA 2 Word Count (W) (14 bit, 1..4000h)
40000DCh - DMA3CNT_L - DMA 3 Word Count (W) (16 bit, 1..10000h)
Specifies the number of data units to be transferred, each unit is 16bit or
32bit depending on the transfer type, a value of zero is treated as max length
(ie. 4000h, or 10000h for DMA3).

40000BAh - DMA0CNT_H - DMA 0 Control (R/W)
40000C6h - DMA1CNT_H - DMA 1 Control (R/W)
40000D2h - DMA2CNT_H - DMA 2 Control (R/W)
40000DEh - DMA3CNT_H - DMA 3 Control (R/W)

  Bit   Expl.
  0-4   Not used
  5-6   Dest Addr Control  (0=Increment,1=Decrement,2=Fixed,3=Increment/Reload)
  7-8   Source Adr Control (0=Increment,1=Decrement,2=Fixed,3=Prohibited)
  9     DMA Repeat                   (0=Off, 1=On) (Must be zero if Bit 11 set)
  10    DMA Transfer Type            (0=16bit, 1=32bit)
  11    Game Pak DRQ  - DMA3 only -  (0=Normal, 1=DRQ <from> Game Pak, DMA3)
  12-13 DMA Start Timing  (0=Immediately, 1=VBlank, 2=HBlank, 3=Special)
          The 'Special' setting (Start Timing=3) depends on the DMA channel:
          DMA0=Prohibited, DMA1/DMA2=Sound FIFO, DMA3=Video Capture
  14    IRQ upon end of Word Count   (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  15    DMA Enable                   (0=Off, 1=On)

After changing the Enable bit from 0 to 1, wait 2 clock cycles before accessing
any DMA related registers.

When accessing OAM (7000000h) or OBJ VRAM (6010000h) by HBlank Timing, then the
"H-Blank Interval Free" bit in DISPCNT register must be set.

Source and Destination Address and Word Count Registers
The SAD, DAD, and CNT_L registers are holding the initial start addresses, and
initial length. The hardware does NOT change the content of these registers
during or after the transfer.
The actual transfer takes place by using internal pointer/counter registers.
The initial values are copied into internal regs under the following
circumstances:
Upon DMA Enable (Bit 15) changing from 0 to 1: Reloads SAD, DAD, CNT_L.
Upon Repeat: Reloads CNT_L, and optionally DAD (Increment+Reload).

DMA Repeat bit
If the Repeat bit is cleared: The Enable bit is automatically cleared after the
specified number of data units has been transferred.
If the Repeat bit is set: The Enable bit remains set after the transfer, and
the transfer will be restarted each time when the Start condition (eg. HBlank,
Fifo) becomes true. The specified number of data units is transferred
<each> time when the transfer is (re-)started. The transfer will be
repeated forever, until it gets stopped by software.

Sound DMA (FIFO Timing Mode) (DMA1 and DMA2 only)
In this mode, the DMA Repeat bit must be set, and the destination address must
be FIFO_A (040000A0h) or FIFO_B (040000A4h).
Upon DMA request from sound controller, 4 units of 32bits (16 bytes) are
transferred (both Word Count register and DMA Transfer Type bit are ignored).
The destination address will not be incremented in FIFO mode.
Keep in mind that DMA channels of higher priority may offhold sound DMA. For
example, when using a 64 kHz sample rate, 16 bytes of sound DMA data are
requested each 0.25ms (4 kHz), at this time another 16 bytes are still in the
FIFO so that there's still 0.25ms time to satisfy the DMA request. Thus DMAs
with higher priority should not be operated for longer than 0.25ms. (This
problem does not arise for HBlank transfers as HBlank time is limited to
16.212us.)

Game Pak DMA
Only DMA 3 may be used to transfer data to/from Game Pak ROM or Flash ROM - it
cannot access Game Pak SRAM though (as SRAM data bus is limited to 8bit units).
In normal mode, DMA is requested as long until Word Count becomes zero. When
setting the 'Game Pack DRQ' bit, then the cartridge must contain an external
circuit which outputs a /DREQ signal. Note that there is only one pin for /DREQ
and /IREQ, thus the cartridge may not supply /IREQs while using DRQ mode.

Video Capture Mode (DMA3 only)
Intended to copy a bitmap from memory (or from external hardware/camera) to
VRAM. When using this transfer mode, set the repeat bit, and write the number
of data units (per scanline) to the word count register. Capture works similar
like HBlank DMA, however, the transfer is started when VCOUNT=2, it is then
repeated each scanline, and it gets stopped when VCOUNT=162.

Transfer End
The DMA Enable flag (Bit 15) is automatically cleared upon completion of the
transfer. The user may also clear this bit manually in order to stop the
transfer (obviously this is possible for Sound/Blanking DMAs only, in all other
cases the CPU is stopped until the transfer completes by itself).

Transfer Rate/Timing
Except for the first data unit, all units are transferred by sequential reads
and writes. For n data units, the DMA transfer time is:

  2N+2(n-1)S+xI

Of which, 1N+(n-1)S are read cycles, and the other 1N+(n-1)S are write cycles,
actual number of cycles depends on the waitstates and bus-width of the source
and destination areas (as described in CPU Instruction Cycle Times chapter).
Internal time for DMA processing is 2I (normally), or 4I (if both source and
destination are in gamepak memory area).

I found no blockers or major issues. I merged `main` into the branch in a scratch worktree with no conflicts. On that merged tree `cargo test` passed (95 tests) and the wasm release build succeeded. The subset grade scored 1.0 on `dma-priority`, `mgba-dma`, `aw-arm-alu`, `aw-thumb-alu`, `memory` and `timer-reload`. `tonc-snd1` scored 0.9917 for video and 0.0 for audio, and the audio score is 0 because Phase 4 (sound) hasn't started.

**Ownership:** `git diff main...phase2/dma` touches only `src/dma.rs`, which the DMA role owns. The two-dot diff also shows `NOTES.md`, `cpu/mod.rs`, `gba.rs`, `io.rs`, `irq.rs` and `timer.rs`, but those changes only exist because `main` has moved on since the branch was cut. They are not edits made on the branch.

**Matches gbatek (GBA DMA Transfers):**
- Address masks: 27-bit for the DMA0 source and DMA0-2 destinations, 28-bit otherwise.
- Word count: 14 or 16 bits, and 0 means the maximum.
- Copying SAD, DAD and CNT_L into the internal registers when Enable goes from 0 to 1.
- On repeat: CNT_L is reloaded, and DAD only in Increment/Reload mode.
- FIFO mode: always 4 words of 32 bits, destination fixed, Word Count and Transfer Type ignored.
- Priority: DMA0 first.
- Timing: 2N+2(n-1)S plus 2I, or 4I when both ends are in the Game Pak.
- Bit 11 of CNT_H is kept on DMA3 only.

**Findings:**

- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/dma.rs:265`: [minor] SRAM is kept readable as a DMA source, which contradicts gbatek "Game Pak DMA". The reason given is that the graded `mgba-dma` rows need it. That is allowed, because the grader's outputs are a permitted source and this doesn't branch on which ROM is loaded. But it is a deliberate departure from the spec. Suggested fix: the integrator should log it in `NOTES.md` as a decision.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/dma.rs:218`: [minor] SAD, DAD and CNT_L read back as 0 instead of open bus. This could matter for the `mgba-io-read` gate test. Suggested fix: the integrator should decide, together with the open-bus work in `bus.rs`. A contract note is enough for now.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/dma.rs:341`: [minor] A source in Game Pak ROM is forced to increment, whatever the source control bits say. This is reasoned from gbatek "ROM Chip" (around line 3915 of the spec: the ROM chip increments its own address on sequential reads), not stated directly in the DMA chapter. The reasoning holds. Suggested fix: cite that section by name in the comment.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/dma.rs:161`: [minor] The "wait 2 clock cycles" start delay is modelled as one CPU step. It is marked with a `ponytail:` comment.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/dma.rs:315`: [minor] Each transfer runs to completion in one go, so a higher-priority channel cannot interrupt one already in progress. Video capture (DMA3 special timing) is not implemented (line 195). Both are marked with `ponytail:` comments and are acceptable for this phase.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/dma.rs:385`: [minor] Repeat combined with Immediate timing still turns the channel off after one transfer. The comment marks this as a choice, and gbatek gives no restart condition for it. Fine as is.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/dma.rs:236`: [minor] The `_ =>` catch-all sends every other offset to `write_control`. It is only correct because `io.rs` always passes even offsets. Suggested fix: match `CNT_H` explicitly and leave the remaining case empty.

**Per-ROM hacks:** none. Test ROM names appear only in comments that explain guessed behaviour.

**Originality:** the naming and structure follow the gbatek register layout. Nothing refers to another emulator, and there are no unexplained magic tables.

**Tests:** 7 unit tests cover:
- immediate copies, their cycle count and the end-of-transfer IRQ
- decrement and fixed address control
- HBlank repeat with destination reload
- channel priority
- FIFO requests
- the zero count and the DMA0 address mask
- an unreadable source repeating the last value
